title: Ulyana and the Vector
premise: Theo Voss smuggles stolen memories through orbital customs and keeps a lonely beacon lit at the system's edge, until gravity stutters for nine seconds and the beacon transmits something impossible: a full sensory record of a massacre aboard the station Meridian, wiped from every archive. Hunted by customs enforcers who insist no such station ever existed, Theo joins forces with Ulyana Reyes, a disgraced customs auditor whose own memories have been edited to hide her role in the cover-up. Together they trace the erased station's survivors into the belt, discovering that the nine-second flicker was a weapon test disguised as an accident. In the end, Theo must choose between broadcasting the massacre record—destroying their own livelihood and likely their life—or trading it back to the corporation for safe passage; they broadcast it, Ulyana takes the fall that keeps Theo free, and the truth finally belongs to everyone.
about_author: Silas Okonkwo is a former radio engineer from Lagos who writes science fiction about people who keep systems running after everyone else has stopped looking. He lives above a decommissioned relay station and insists the hum helps him think.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs is interrupted when gravity fails for exactly nine seconds across the whole system; Theo's beacon at the edge of nowhere captures a burst of data during the blackout. The emotional beat is unease—the sense that the universe just blinked and only Theo noticed.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Still Theo's POV. Examining the burst, Theo finds a complete sensory recording: screaming, vacuum, a station called Meridian dying. But Meridian appears in no registry, and customs flags the beacon as unlicensed contraband. The beat is dread hardening into resolve as Theo decides not to delete the file.

chapters.title: Auditor Down
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Disgraced customs auditor Ulyana Reyes recognizes the beacon's signature—it matches equipment she signed off on years ago, before her memory was edited. She defects from her own investigation to find its source. The beat is bitter self-doubt curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Ulyana meet hostile and suspicious in a belt dive bar, each convinced the other is corporate bait; a customs raid forces them to flee together with the memory core. The beat is reluctant alliance forged under fire.

chapters.title: What the Records Deny
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hiding in a derelict refinery, Ulyana decrypts fragments proving Meridian housed four thousand people—and that her own edited memories contain the order authorizing its erasure. The beat is horror at discovering you were complicit in your own forgetting.

chapters.title: The Belt Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following a survivor's trail, they find Meridian refugees living off-grid, who confirm the massacre but refuse to testify, terrified of the weapon that caused the gravity flicker. The beat is grief meeting cowardice, and understanding both.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The corporation's fixer offers Theo a trade: the memory core for wealth, amnesty, and a new identity—while Ulyana secretly negotiates to take sole blame if they surrender instead. The beat is temptation, and the slow realization that every offer is a lie wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: The Weapon in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They infiltrate the testing platform where the gravity weapon is being refined and learn the flicker was a calibration shot—the next target is the refugee settlement. The beat is cold clarity: survival for some has been purchased with erasure of others.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, climax. With enforcers boarding and the weapon charging, Theo uses the beacon itself—one final unauthorized transmission—to push the massacre record into every public feed in the system as the platform burns around them. The beat is terror transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: Belonging to Everyone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. The broadcast ignites scandal; Ulyana surrenders to protect Theo, while Theo, stripped of smuggling and beacon alike, joins the refugee settlement rebuilding Meridian's memory from scattered minds. The final beat is bittersweet belonging: justice achieved outside the law, paid for in separation, and worth it.
